title: Realizing Kan fibrations and comparing Kan homotopy groups
statement: Use simplicial sets, horns, Kan complexes and realization as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and k-spaces as in [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]. Call $p:X\to Y$ a Kan fibration if it has the right lifting property against $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for all $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. A Serre fibration of k-spaces means a map with the right lifting property against $D^m\times\{0\}\hookrightarrow D^m\times[0,1]$ for all $m\geq0$. The realization of every Kan fibration is a Serre fibration; neither $X$ nor $Y$ is assumed Kan. For a Kan complex $K$, its simplicial components (vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by edges) map bijectively to $\pi_0(|K|)$. For a vertex $x$ of $K$ and $n\geq1$, define $\pi_n^s(K,x)$ using simplicial maps $\Delta^n/\partial\Delta^n\to K$ sending the collapsed boundary to $x$, modulo the equivalence relation generated by based simplicial homotopies with cylinder $(-)\times\Delta^1$, with the group operation given by Kan horn composition. Realization gives natural group isomorphisms $\pi_n^s(K,x)\cong\pi_n(|K|,x)$, compatible with pointed simplicial maps.

source.place: Corollary 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.6.3, with §3.4 simplicial homotopy groups. No Stacks tag for the realization-of-fibrations theorem.

proof.text: First consider any simplicial map $r:U\to V$ lifting against all boundary inclusions. Dimension zero makes $r_0$ surjective, so this is a trivial Kan fibration in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. Its graph $i=(1_U,r):U\to U\times V$ is degreewise injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to $i$, the upper map $1_U$ and lower map $\operatorname{pr}_2$, obtaining $h:U\times V\to U$ with $hi=1_U$ and $rh=\operatorname{pr}_2$. Realization identifies $|U\times V|$ with the product of realizations. For a Serre lifting problem $a:D^m\to|U|$, $b:D^m\times[0,1]\to|V|$, the formula $\widetilde b(z,t)=|h|(a(z),b(z,t))$ is continuous, equals $a$ at $t=0$, and lies over $b$. Thus $|r|$ is a Serre fibration, without any fibrancy assumption on $U,V$.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.5, with the graph lifting and retract argument written out; product preservation in Lemma 3.1.8

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-kan-minimal-factorization] to the given Kan fibration $p:X\to Y$. It gives $p=qr$ with $r$ lifting against all boundaries and with $q$ a Kan fibration trivial over each simplex. Step 1 makes $|r|$ Serre and [lem-coef-kan-locally-trivial-realization] makes $|q|$ Serre. To lift a disk homotopy along $|p|$, first lift it along $|q|$ starting at $|r|a$, and then along $|r|$ starting at $a$. The second lift lies over the first, so their composite is the required lift for $|p|$. This proves the first assertion for arbitrary $X,Y$, including empty fibres.

Let $A$ be the vertices of $K$ modulo the equivalence relation generated by edges. All vertices of any simplex have the same class because its one-dimensional faces connect them. Hence the simplices with vertices in a fixed $a\in A$ form a simplicial subset $K_a$, and $K=\coprod_{a\in A}K_a$. Realization preserves this coproduct, so $|K|$ is the topological disjoint union of the $|K_a|$. Each point in $|K_a|$ is joined inside its representing simplex to a vertex, and all its vertices are connected by realized edge chains. Thus every $|K_a|$ is path connected and nonempty, and different summands cannot be joined by a path. This gives exactly the stated bijection $A\cong\pi_0(|K|)$, also when $K$ is empty; it is natural on vertices.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.3; the argument applies even without a Kan hypothesis

proof.text: For $n\geq1$, realize a representative $\alpha:\Delta^n\to K$ constant on the boundary. The realized simplex pair is $(D^n,S^{n-1})$, so it represents a based topological $n$-sphere and gives a map $\rho_n:\pi_n^s(K,x)\to\pi_n(|K|,x)$. A generating based simplicial homotopy realizes to a based continuous homotopy because realization preserves products, colimits and the interval $|\Delta^1|=[0,1]$. Therefore the map descends through the equivalence relation generated by these homotopies. This also identifies the formulation with maps from $\Delta^n/\partial\Delta^n$: a based map from that quotient is exactly such an $\alpha$, and products with $\Delta^1$ are computed degreewise. Postcomposition commutes with all these operations, so $\rho_n$ is natural. Write $\rho_0$ for step 3.

source.place: Definition 3.4.4; explicit representative description following Proposition 3.6.3

proof.text: Use the concrete $P_xK$, $q$ and $\Omega_xK$ from [lem-coef-kan-path-boundary-bijections]. Its boundary-lifting assertion gives a contraction of $P_xK$ fixing $c_x$: prescribe $1$ and the constant $c_x$ at the two ends of $P_xK\times\Delta^1$ and the constant $c_x$ on $\{c_x\}\times\Delta^1$. This prescription agrees on overlaps and the inclusion of that union is degreewise injective. Dimension zero and the trivial-Kan definition allow the monomorphism lifting lemma to extend it to the whole cylinder. After realization this is a based contraction of $|P_xK|$. The Kan fibration $q$ realizes to a Serre fibration by step 2, and preservation of pullbacks identifies its fibre over $x$ with $|\Omega_xK|$. Apply the natural Serre homotopy sequence. Since the total space is based contractible, its boundary maps are bijections $\delta_j^t:\pi_{j+1}(|K|,x)\to\pi_j(|\Omega_xK|,c_x)$ for $j\geq1$. For $j=0$, the component action is transitive because the total space is connected, and its stabilizer is zero because its fundamental group is zero. The orbit map from $\pi_1(|K|,x)$ to the fibre components is therefore a bijection as well. These topological bijections are natural for pointed maps of $K$. The disk-lift maps of [lem-coef-serre-disk-lift-boundary-bijection] apply to this based contraction and this Serre fibration, so choose $\delta_j^t$ with exactly its last-face convention. That statement supplies the representative formula, lift independence and naturality for this choice, including the initial-endpoint convention at $j=0$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.6.3, based contraction from boundary lifting; Lemma 2.4.16 and the low-degree fibre-component action

proof.text: For every $j\geq0$, compare the simplicial boundary map $\delta_j^s$ with the continuous last-face boundary $\delta_j^t$ chosen in step 5. Take a representative $\alpha:\Delta^{j+1}\to K$ constant at $x$ on its boundary. The path-boundary node supplies a lift $\gamma:\Delta^{j+1}\to P_xK$ with $q\gamma=\alpha$ and $\gamma=c_x$ on $\Lambda_{j+1}^{j+1}$; it defines $\delta_j^s[\alpha]=[d_{j+1}\gamma]$. Realization preserves the displayed equality and every face restriction, hence $|\gamma|$ is a permissible continuous lift of $|\alpha|$ in [lem-coef-serre-disk-lift-boundary-bijection]. That node's explicit formula gives $\delta_j^t\rho_{j+1}[\alpha]=[|d_{j+1}\gamma|]=\rho_j\delta_j^s[\alpha]$. The same ordered face and simplex/disk identifications are used on both sides, so no orientation reversal is silently inserted. When $j=0$, both constructions take the initial endpoint of a lift whose terminal endpoint is $c_x$. Independence of continuous lifts is now an explicit clause of the cited node, rather than being inferred from the bare existence of a natural exact sequence.

source.place: Representative compatibility left to the reader after Proposition 3.6.3, supplied here by realizing the chosen horn lift

proof.text: Induct simultaneously over all pointed Kan complexes on $n$. The base $n=0$ is step 3. If $\rho_j$ is bijective for every pointed Kan complex, then it is bijective for $(\Omega_xK,c_x)$, which is Kan by the path-boundary lemma. In the square of step 6 both horizontal maps are bijections, by that lemma and step 5. Thus $\rho_{j+1}=(\delta_j^t)^{-1}\rho_j\delta_j^s$ is a bijection. This proves the comparison in every degree without a boundedness or connectedness assumption.

source.place: Induction in the proof of Proposition 3.6.3

proof.text: For pointed $n$-simplices $\alpha,\beta$, $n\geq1$, fill the horn in dimension $n+1$ with faces $d_{n+1}w=\alpha$, $d_{n-1}w=\beta$, all other prescribed faces constant at $x$, and missing face $d_n$. Intersections agree because both representatives have constant boundaries. The Kan condition gives $w$ and the horn product is $d_nw$. Here is the continuous disk relation. Write $F_i$ for the geometric face opposite vertex $i$ in the standard $(n+1)$-simplex, and $H=\bigcup_{i\ne n}F_i$. Choose a point $z$ just outside $F_n$ with barycentric coordinate $z_n<0$ and $z_i>0$ for $i\ne n$. For $u\in F_n$, follow the ray from $z$ through $u$ to its last intersection $r(u)$ with the simplex. It lies in $H$. This radial map is a homeomorphism $F_n\to H$ fixing their common boundary: each ray enters through $F_n$ and exits through $H$, and the inverse meets the plane $t_n=0$. Its exit parameter is the minimum of the positive affine-coordinate exit times, so the map and inverse are continuous, including at boundary points where the exit equals the entry. The affine homotopy $(1-t)u+t r(u)$ stays inside the simplex and fixes $\partial F_n$. Composing it with $|w|$ therefore compares the missing-face representative with the map on the horn disk relative to its boundary. On this horn disk, every face other than $F_{n+1}$ and $F_{n-1}$ maps constantly to $x$, as does every boundary of these two faces. Collapsing those constant pieces gives the pinch to $S^n\vee S^n$: each of the two active face disks has its own boundary collapsed. These are two sphere summands, not two disks glued along their entire boundary. The radial cell parametrization traverses the $F_{n+1}$ summand followed by $F_{n-1}$, and their orientations agree with that of the missing face, since their boundary signs $(-1)^{n+1},(-1)^{n-1}$ are opposite to $(-1)^n$. Thus this pinch represents concatenation in the first cube coordinate. For $n=1$ the homotopy is exactly the replacement of edge $02$ by edges $01$ followed by $12$, preserving their order even for a noncommutative fundamental group; in higher dimensions the same two adjacent face disks give the two halves of the concatenation cube after their constant boundary pieces are collapsed. Consequently $\rho_n[d_nw]=\rho_n[\alpha]\rho_n[\beta]$. Since $\rho_n$ is bijective by step 7, this equality makes the product independent of fillers and representatives and transports the identity, inverse and associative laws from the topological group. Step 4 already proves naturality.

source.place: Final paragraph after Proposition 3.6.3; horn-composition compatibility extended in the same disk relation to all positive degrees
